Regulations/18.— In exercise of the powers conferred on it under sub-sections (1) and clause (i) of sub-section (2) of Section 85 of the Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, 2016, the Maharashtra Real Estate Regulatory Authority hereby makes the following Regulations :—

CHAPTER 1
GENERAL
1. Short title, object, commencement and extent.—(1) These regulations may be called the Maharashtra Real Estate Regulatory Authority (General) Regulations, 2017.
(2) The object of these Regulations is to establish procedures regarding the general functioning of the Authority and for the conduct of business of the Authority.
(3) These Regulations shall come into force on the date of their notification in the Official Gazette.
(4) These Regulations shall apply in relation to all matters falling within the jurisdiction of the Authority in the State of Maharashtra.

2. Definitions.—(1) In these Regulations, unless the context otherwise requires,—
(a) “Act” means the Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, 2016 as amended from time to time;
(b) “Adjudication” means the process of arriving at decisions on complaints submitted to the Authority or the Adjudicating Officer under section 31 of the Act;
(c) “Chairperson” means the Chairperson of the Authority;
(d) “Authority” means the Maharashtra Real Estate Regulatory Authority;

3. Formats of Certificates of Architect, Engineer and Chartered Accountant.—The certificates issued by the project architect, project engineer, chartered accountant and submitted to the banks for getting release of money from the separate account shall be in Forms 1, 2 and 3 respectively. The certificate issued by the project architect on completion of each of the building/wing of the real estate project shall be in Form 4.

4. Additional Disclosures by Promoters on the Website and Project site.—In addition to all the details of the proposed Real Estate project, to be uploaded by the promoter on his webpage on the website of the Authority, as required under sub-section (1) of section 11 of the Act and clause (1) and (2) of Rule 3 of the Maharashtra Real Estate (Regulation and Development) (Registration of Real Estate Projects, Registration of Real Estate Agents, Rates of Interest and Disclosures on Website) Rules, 2017, the promoter shall additionally upload the following details :—
(a) The annual report on statement of accounts, in Form 5 [issued in accordance with the third proviso to section 4(2)(l) of the Act] duly certified and signed by the chartered accountant who is the statutory auditor of the promoter’s enterprise.—
Explanation 1 : The chartered accountant certifying the progress of the registered real estate project for the purpose of withdrawal of amounts from the separate account should be a different entity than the chartered accountant who is the statutory auditor of the promoter’s enterprise.
Explanation 2 : If the Form 5 issued by the statutory auditor reveals that any certificate issued by the project architect, engineer or the chartered accountant has false or incorrect information and the amounts collected for a particular project have not been utilized for the project and the withdrawal has not been in compliance with the proportion to the percentage of completion of the project, the Authority, in addition to taking penal actions as contemplated in the Act and the Rules, shall also take up the matter with the concerned regulatory body of the said professionals of the architect, engineer or chartered accountant, for necessary penal action against them, including dis-memberment.

16. Orders issued or action taken by the Secretary or Officers in the Authority may, at any time, be reviewed, revoked, revised, modified, amended, altered or otherwise changed by the Chairperson on an application made by any interested or affected party or suo motu by the Chairperson.
17. Any functions required by these Regulations to be performed by the Secretary may, with the approval of the Authority, be delegated by the Secretary to any other Officer of the Authority.
18. Meetings.—Save for the adjudicatory proceedings of the Authority, this section shall apply to the meetings of the Authority.
19. Quorum for the meetings of the Authority shall be two.
20. If within half an hour after the time appointed for a meeting of the Authority, a quorum is not present, the meeting shall stand adjourned to such date, time and place as the Chairperson may determine.
21. The Chairperson shall preside over the meetings and conduct the business. Members stationed at Benches, outside Mumbai, may participate in the meetings through video conferencing. If the Chairperson is unable to be present in the meetings for any reason, or where there is no Chairperson, the senior most Member present shall preside at the meeting.
22. (a) All questions which come up before any meetings of the Authority shall be decided by a majority of votes of the Members present and voting. In the event of an equality of votes, the Chairperson or in his absence, the Member presiding shall have a second or casting vote.
(b) Save as otherwise provided in these Regulations, every Member shall have one vote.
23. (a) The Secretary or in his absence an Officer of the Authority designated by the Chairperson, shall record the minutes of the meetings and maintain a register which will, amongst other things, contain the names and designation of Members and invitees present in the meeting, a record of proceedings and notes of dissent, if any. The draft minutes shall, as soon as practicable, be sent to the Chairperson and the attending Members.
(b) The decision taken in a meeting of the Authority shall be recorded in the minutes in a clear and concise manner, along with reasons. In case the minutes record any statement/submission made by an invitee, a copy of the minutes shall be sent to such invitee.
(c) The minutes of the previous meeting shall be confirmed by circulation or at the next meeting of the Authority.
24. Adjudication proceedings.—For adjudication proceedings with respect to complaints filed with the Authority, the Authority may, by order, direct that specific matters or issues be heard and decided by a single bench of either the Chairperson or any Member of the Authority.
25. Vacancies, etc., not to invalidate proceedings.—No act or proceedings of the Authority shall be questioned or shall be invalidated merely on the ground of existence of any vacancy or defect in the constitution of the Authority.
26. Authorized Representative.—A person who is a party to any proceedings before the Authority may either appear in person or authorise any other person to present his case before the Authority and to do all or any of the acts for the purpose.
A person who authorises another person to represent him and to act on his behalf before the Authority shall file a Memorandum of Authorisation in Form 6 herein.
In cases under Rule 6(a) of the Maharashtra Real Estate (Regulation and Development) (Registration of Real Estate Projects, Registration of Real Estate Agents, Rates of Interest and Disclosures on Website) Rules, 2017, the terms and conditions subject to which a person may authorize another person to represent, act and plead on his behalf before the Authority shall be determined by the Authority from time to time.

All orders and decisions of the Authority shall be certified by the signature of the Secretary or an officer authorized by the Chairperson, stamped with the official seal of the Authority, and shall be communicated to all parties in the proceedings as expeditiously as possible from the date of passing the order.
29. Commission's Records - Documents, inspection, confidentiality and accessibility.—The Authority shall maintain an indexed directory of its records as expeditiously as feasible, which shall include complaints filed, details of hearings conducted, orders / documents issued from time to time.
30. (a) Subject to sub-regulation (k), the records of the Authority shall be open for inspection to all upon payment of fees and compliance with such conditions as may be determined.
(b) If an applicant applies in Form No. 7, subject to compliance with the conditions and rules and payment of fees as directed by the Authority, the Authority may give certified copies of documents and papers available with the Authority to anyone. To ensure that the Authority responds to requests for supplying certified copies of documents, the Authority shall designate an officer, and within 14 (fourteen) working days from the receipt of the request, shall make an effort to send the certified copies of the requested documents.
(c) The Authority may issue orders that any information, documents and other papers and material in possession of the Authority, being confidential and in special powers, shall not be made available for inspection or giving copies, and the Authority may also direct that such document, paper or material shall not be used in any matter except as specially authorized by the Authority.
31. Information deemed necessary by the Authority, along with other matters, shall be made available for viewing by the public through the Authority's website.
32. Interim orders, inquiry, investigation, collection of information, etc.—The Authority, considering the truth and facts of the case, may grant interim or interlocutory orders at any stage as it deems fit.
33. The Authority, for collection of information, inquiry, investigation, entry, search, seizure, and for other matters, without prejudice to its general powers, may give such directions or orders as it deems fit :—
(a) The Authority may, at any time, direct the Secretary or an officer or officers as it deems fit, to study, investigate or submit information regarding any case within the jurisdiction of the Authority under this Act or rules.
(b) The Authority may give other directions as it deems fit for the above purpose and may specify a time limit for submitting the report or information.
(c) The Authority may itself direct any person to produce books, accounts, etc., before the officers of the Authority, to inspect and keep them, or authorize the Secretary or officers to give such directions.
(d) The Authority may give directions for collecting necessary information, details or documents for discharging its functions mandated by the Act and rules.
(e) If any such report or information received by the Authority appears to be incomplete or half-baked, the Authority or the Secretary or an officer authorized for this purpose may direct further inquiry, report and submission of information.
(f) The Authority may give directions for proceedings in incidental, consequential and supplementary matters that may be related to the above matters.

(b) The application for review shall be filed in the same manner as filing a complaint under these Regulations.
(c) The Authority shall review its directions, decisions or orders with the same powers as vested in a Civil Court under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 for the purpose of review.
(d) If it is found that there is no sufficient ground for review, the Authority shall reject such review application.

37. Continuation of proceedings after death, etc.—(a) When in any proceeding, any party connected with the proceedings dies or is declared insolvent or absconds, the proceedings shall continue with such of the legal heirs, executor, administrator, receiver, liquidator or their legal representatives as the case may be.
(b) If the Authority directs that there is no need to bring legal heirs on record in the proceedings, the Authority shall record the reasons and terminate the proceedings.
(c) If in any proceeding it is necessary to bring a legal heir on record, an application to this effect shall be filed within ninety (90) days from the date of occasion to bring the legal heir on record. 38. Issuing orders and directions.—Subject to the provisions of the Act, Acts and Regulations, the Authority may issue orders, directions and procedural instructions from time to time regarding the implementation of the Regulations and continue the procedure to be followed on matters in the Regulations.
39. Protection of inherent powers of the Authority.—The inherent powers of the Authority to issue orders necessary for rendering justice in any case and to prevent abuse of the process of the Authority shall not be limited by anything contained in these Regulations.

40. The Authority shall not be barred from adopting a simplified procedure with summary procedure for proceedings in respect of any case or class of cases having special circumstances consistent with the Act or rules, but differing from the provisions of these Regulations, after noting reasons therefor, keeping in view that the special circumstances of any case or class of cases are consistent with the procedure in the Act or Rules.
41. In respect of any matters for which no regulations have been made, while conducting proceedings or exercising powers, the Authority shall not be barred by these Regulations, and the Authority shall conduct proceedings in such manner as it deems fit in accordance with the powers and functions under the Act.
42. General power to amend / rectify.—The Authority may at any time, on such terms as to costs or otherwise as it deems fit, make all necessary amendments, rectifications for the determination of the real question or issue arising in the proceedings, including any clerical or arithmetical error in any order passed by the Authority or any other error in subsequent proceedings:
Provided that, if the Authority considers it necessary to make amendments or rectifications for resolving the real question or issue arising before the Authority, the Authority shall give an opportunity of making a representation on such amendments or rectifications to the affected parties in relation to the real question or issue.
43. Power to remove difficulties.—If any difficulty arises in giving effect to the Regulations, the Authority may, by general or special order, do anything not inconsistent with the provisions of this Act for the purpose of removing the difficulty, as may be necessary and expedient.
44. Extension or abridgment of time prescribed.—Subject to the provisions of the Act or the rules, the time prescribed by these Regulations or by any order given by the Authority for doing any act (whether already expired or not) may be extended or abridged by the Authority by an order giving sufficient reasons therefor.
45. Effect of non-compliance.—Non-compliance with any provision of these Regulations shall not render any proceeding invalid merely on the ground of such non-compliance, unless the Authority is satisfied that such non-compliance has resulted in a miscarriage of justice.
46. Costs.—(a) Subject to such conditions and limitations as may be directed by the Authority, the costs of and incidental to all proceedings shall be awarded at the discretion of the Authority, and the Authority shall have full power to determine by whom, out of which funds, and to what extent such costs are to be paid, and to give proper directions for the aforesaid purposes.
(b) The costs shall be paid within thirty (30) days from the date of the order or within such period as may be specified by the Authority by order. If a party makes default in paying the costs within the permitted period, the Authority shall issue a decree/order of a Civil Court for payment of costs in connection therewith.
47. Administrative charges and general fee.—In accordance with the provisions of Rule 3(7) of the Maharashtra Real Estate (Regulation and Development) (Registration of Real Estate Projects, Registration of Real Estate Agents, Rates of Interest and Disclosures on Website) Rules, 2017, if any real estate project withdraws from project registration, administrative charges / fees of rupees five thousand only shall be retained by the Authority itself. The remaining amount of the registration fee shall be refunded to the promoter within 15 days through RTGS, NEFT or any other transaction mode.
48.
